title: NeuralSat raises $3.2m pre-seed on 72-satellite 50Gbps data relay & processing constellation
html:
German space startup NeuralSat GmbH has announced a €2.9 million ($3.2m) pre-seed funding round to develop a 72-satellite space data relay and processing constellation.

The company is proposing 50 Gbps speeds and onboard computing capability, without mentioning optical downlink capability.

The round, led by Capnamic Ventures and Bayern Kapital, will fund an in-orbit demonstration to fly in 2027, before beginning deployment in 2028.

“We believe the next major evolution in space will … come from connecting satellites to shared infrastructure that enables them to communicate, access computing resources, and operate together,” said chief executive Mohd Bilal. “Just as the Internet transformed how computers interact on Earth, we intend to transform how intelligence is connected and delivered in space.”

Würzburg-based NeuralSat emphasizes the utility of making the most of the in-orbit data economy, stressing the need for more robust relay infrastructure in low-Earth orbit (LEO), while providing hosted payload space and a suite of pooled compute resources for customers aboard “NeuralSat nodes” which can downlink to “available ground stations.”

The company describes using optical and high-frequency radio links, which could mean redundancy on intersatellite connectivity between NeuralSat nodes, but probably implies optical intersatellite links (ISLs) and radio frequency downlink, which is the existing norm for leading LEO constellations. Optical downlink is a challenging technology requiring mild weather and specialized optical receivers, mostly spoken of today in performance demonstrations to advanced portable terminals.

While optical downlink receivers are under construction worldwide at landmark ground stations, experts do not expect it to eclipse RF transmission, as optical ISLs have in orbit. In early November, phased array antenna builder Northwood Space Corp closed a $375mn Series C to accelerate the development of RF downlink, suggesting investors remain confident in the slower, more weather-tolerant method.

Like OwlO cloud, another ODC startup in neighboring Luxembourg, which emerged from stealth in early November, NeuralSat has avoided grandiose claims of rendering terrestrial compute obsolete, and has made no promises about unleashing self-sustaining space AI, like many US-based ODC companies.

Since leading constellations use their own ISLs and have longstanding relationships with the ground stations they use, in some cases owning them outright, NeuralSat’s business case shines brightest in its hosted payload space, housing customers looking to access orbit while furnishing them with a data relay network and compute resources as part of the same package.

The offering is tailored for non-space companies, who are often tempted by big tech LEO giants due to the low prices associated with their economies of scale. With the “fortress Europe” mindset taking hold across the continent, players have been eager to diversify away from international partners.

At Space Tech Expo Europe in Bremen last week, countless European spokespeople voiced sovereign arguments as if they were forgone, inarguable conclusions. Benjamin Kawak, vice president of sales and growth at Atmos Space Cargo, told attendees: “We might be locating a cost advantage when [buying overseas], but dependency will always have its own costs in the end.”

NeuralSat recently signed an MoU with Atmos to explore the use of NeuralSat’s in-orbit data processing and relay capabilities on an Atmos Phoenix 2 mission planned for 2028. Neuron-0, NeuralSat’s first in-orbit demonstration mission, is planned for launch in Q4 2027.

NeuralSat is a member of the European Space Agency’s Business Incubation Center (ESA BIC), and the Nvidia Inception Program. Its pre-seed round enjoyed participation from ZOHO.VC, Robin Capital, KIEMIS Holding, and Mission E Capital.
summary: Startup offers European compute-ready orbital access and data network to unlock LEO power in the EU
